rubric.2: Application implements user registration supporting admin, nurse, and physician roles.
rubric.5: Application persists all user accounts, role data, hospital units, beds, encounters, and patient board information using a durable, database-backed storage system.
rubric.6: Application implements a hospital unit structure allowing admins to define and store named units (e.g., ICU, ER, 3A).
rubric.7: Application implements bed management within each unit by defining beds and storing their associated metadata.
rubric.8: Application supports assigning patients to beds through encounter records.
rubric.9: Application displays a live-updating patient board shared across all connected users.
rubric.10: Application synchronizes all edits—including patient statuses, notes, and tasks—in real time for all users without requiring page refreshes.
rubric.11: Application allows multiple users to edit the board simultaneously without conflicts.
rubric.12: Application displays presence indicators showing which users are currently online.
rubric.13: Application displays a bed card that shows the patient's name.
rubric.14: Application displays a bed card that shows the patient's MRN.
rubric.15: Application displays a bed card that shows the patient's age or date of birth.
rubric.16: Application displays a bed card that shows the assigned nurse.
rubric.17: Application displays a bed card that shows the patient’s current status.
rubric.18: Application displays a bed card that shows a preview of patient notes.
rubric.19: Application displays a bed card that shows the number of tasks completed and the total number of assigned tasks.
rubric.20: Application allows admins to manage hospital units, including creating, editing, and deleting them.
rubric.21: Application allows admins to manage beds within units, including creating, editing, and deleting them.
rubric.22: Application allows admins to manage user accounts, including creation, modification, and deactivation.
rubric.23: Application persists all board data, patient information, and administrative configurations in the database to ensure full durability across sessions.
rubric.24: Application implements a public forum chat room accessible to all authenticated admins, nurses, and physicians.
rubric.25: Application allows eligible users to post messages to the public forum chat.
rubric.26: Application displays clear sender attribution for each message, including user name, role, and timestamp.
rubric.27: Application updates all chat messages in real time for every connected user without requiring page reloads.
rubric.28: Application maintains a scrollable history of recent chat messages so users can review prior discussion.
rubric.29: Application implements an emergency alert banner system allowing admins to create alerts with at least a title and message, and optional severity or category metadata.
rubric.30: Application broadcasts newly created emergency alerts instantly to all connected users.
rubric.31: Application displays all active emergency alerts as prominent banners within the application interface.
rubric.32: Application ensures each emergency alert remains visible to a user until they explicitly dismiss it.
rubric.33: Application persists active alerts so that users who connect after an alert is created still see all undismissed alerts.
